Subject: MeadowHealth on-prem preflight — initial site inventory attached

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the call this morning — attached is our current site inventory (hardware, rack IDs, basic network blocks). We want to get Redwood deployed inside our VPC-owned cluster in Q4 and need to validate any network and IO requirements up front so we can coordinate with our on-site team and the datacenter.

High level asks:
- What firewall ports / egress IPs do you need open to Redwood control plane and runtime?
- Do you have specific MTU or fragmentation requirements we should validate with the WAN team?
- Storage: we plan to have an NVMe-backed local tier for KV/cache and a separate blockstore for model artifacts. Any minimum IOPS or throughput guidance?
- Encryption & retention: we use customer-managed KMS and have SOC2 controls — do you need anything extra for key rotation/audit?

Attached: meadow_health_site_inventory.xlsx

Can you share a short intake checklist we can run against our site ops? We can get a network diagram and topology exported this week.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Ops
MeadowHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Alex — thanks for the inventory, got it. I pulled a few notes together and attached our preflight intake checklist (short version) so your site team can run through it. Key items we need answers for before scheduling a hands-on run: 

1) Networking
- Egress: list of public egress IPs (if NATed) or explicit ranges for our control plane so we can create allowlists.
- Ports: outbound 443 to control plane, 2197/tcp for internal cluster agent telemetry (we can tunnel if security requires), and 10250/2379 etc only if you want direct kube API access from Redwood support. We'll note exact port list in the doc.
- MTU: we recommend 1500 for simplicity; if the WAN requires jumbo frames call it out and we'll provide kernel tuning steps.
- VLANs: which VLANs will be used for pod traffic, storage/VLANs for blockstore, and management. Provide VLAN IDs and gateway IPs.

2) Storage/IO
- Workload sizing: tell us expected concurrent inference QPS, average sequence length, and model sizes for a first-pass estimate.
- KV/cache: recommend local NVMe per GPU node (min 350–500 MB/s sustained per NVMe for caching heavy seqs).
- Artifact store: object-blockstore (S3-compatible) or host-attached blockstore? If blockstore, we need minimum 200 MB/s write throughput for model pulls during scale-up windows — if you plan large rolling updates, higher burst helps.
- Filesystem: avoid NFS for the model cache unless you can guarantee POSIX semantics and stable throughput; prefer hostPath for cache + replicated artifact store.

3) Security/compliance
- KMS: customer-managed KMS is fine; please provide key ARN and IP ranges for KMS endpoints and whether HSM-backed keys are required.
- Audit: we will forward our agent audit webhook details; let us know if you want audit logs archived to your bucket.

4) Ops/credentials
- A service account for the on-site cluster with cluster-admin for the initial install (we prefer limited lifetime tokens).
- A jump host plan for out-of-band troubleshooting (IP and allowed times).

Next steps: please run the checklist against your local ops team and send back VLAN and egress info plus the network diagram. Tentative timeline: intake + validation this week, planning call early next week. CCing Karthik and Irene for the technical scope.

Attachments: rdw_preflight_intake_checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Alex / Hannah — quick technical clarifications from our infra team so we can size node pools and PV classes: 

- Node pools: given the inventory, we recommend two node pools for the initial rollout: 
  * io-optimized (NVMe) nodes for runtime KV/cache + GPU workloads — 1 NVMe per GPU node, local SSDs with at least 500 GB and ~3.5k–5k IOPS baseline.
  * archive nodes (HDD or SATA) for older model artifacts and logging retention — can be lower IOPS but larger capacity.

- PV performance: if blockstore is provided by the site, please capture a small fio run (randread/randwrite 4k/8k, 32 threads, 60s) and paste throughput/IOPS; we need numbers to decide per-pod PVC limits.

- Network egress patterns: model downloads happen at scale during deploys — plan for ephemeral bursts (per-deploy) of ~300–500 MB/s aggregate for a typical 8-model rollout. If you have a content distribution cache or local object proxy we can dramatically reduce peak load.

- Mounts & filesystem: avoid using a single NFS server for active KV caches. For small test installs NFS is ok but production caching should use local NVMe + optional replication.

- Security: if KMS endpoints are limited to a private VPC endpoint, we'll need the endpoint DNS and cert chain to validate the TLS handshake; otherwise, NATed egress to the cloud KMS is simpler.

I can also run a short validation script remotely if you provide a short-lived kubeconfig and a jump host. Marissa — noting procurement may want to batch the Dedicated capacity ask if they anticipate sustained QPS.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
